newsitem.title: USA: U.S. March S&P 500 ends down, near session low.
newsitem.headline: U.S. March S&P 500 ends down, near session low.

text.p: Dec 30 - U.S. March S&P 500 futures ended down and near their session low, pressured by dealer selling of about 1,000 contracts into a quiet market, traders said. Locals also sellers in afternoon trading, catching early buyers by surprise, they said. March S&P support now at 757.50 and 755.00, trader said.

Overall trade was quiet and futures trading pits were thin as many players remained on vacation for seasonal holidays. S&Ps will hold normal trading hours on Tuesday, while most U.S. markets close early for New Year's Eve. There will be no trade on Wednesday.
March S&Ps began pit trading stronger, but soon pared those gains as T-bonds failed to hold their 114-6/32 session high in March.
March bonds opened up and were firm after November U.S. leading indicators matched forecasts for up 0.1 percent, while October's reported 0.1 percent rise was revised to unchanged.
But gains in bonds and equity futures eroded after slightly stronger than expected November existing home sales and APICS surveys.
Home sales rose 1.8 percent to a 4.04 million unit rate versus a forecast for no change from October's 3.97 million.
The American Production and Inventory Control Society reported its December business outlook index at 51.8 from 46.8 in November.
March S&P 500s stayed above support early at Friday's settlement of 764.60 and Friday's low of 761.20, but slipped below those levels later.
Traders pegged support for Tuesday's session at 757.50 and 755.00.

At settlement, March Russell 2000s ended up 0.20 point to 365.60, Value Lines were off 2.40 point to 689.10, Nikkei 225 index futures lost 50.0 to 19,395.0 and Midcap 400s rose 0.45 point to 257.95. ((--Derivatives Desk: 312-408-8750)) ((email:derivatives@reuters.com))
